Jun (Acme): Hey team — around 03:12 UTC we saw a 2min window of sustained 429s after our EU failover. Customer impact: chat UI frozen. Logs show lots of `429` with Retry-After 60. Any fast ideas?
Maya (Support): Sorry you're hitting this Jun. Can you paste a short sample of the request pattern (concurrency / calls per minute) and whether these were streaming or discrete requests?
Jun (Acme): Mostly short poll-style requests from ~600 simultaneous users. Each poll makes 3 calls in parallel (messages + embeddings + analytics ping). We saw a leader election in EU which caused many clients to reconnect to Redwood endpoint at once.
Tom (SRE): That sounds like a reconnect fanout + parallelism problem. If many clients reconnect and retry without jitter you can hit tenant RPM/TPM. Do you have per-connection keepalives?
Jun (Acme): No keepalives, clients just reconnect on websocket close and immediately resume polling. We have about 18k requests/min at peak after failover.
Rajat (Platform): Quick check: our limits for that tenant are 12k RPM and 600k TPM (per account). If they jumped to 18k RPM for multiple minutes that would trigger 429s. Can you run this query and paste last 5m? `redwood logs query --tenant acme --from -5m --filter "status:429" | head -n 20`
Jun (Acme): Pasted output: 
```
2026-03-17T03:12:23Z tenant=acme status=429 path=/v1/chat tokens=85 rpm=17920 tpm=342000 reason=rate_limit_exceeded
2026-03-17T03:12:24Z tenant=acme status=429 path=/v1/embeddings tokens=0 rpm=17210 tpm=339500 reason=rate_limit_exceeded
... (repeats)
```
Maya (Support): Thanks. Two actionable paths: (1) Short-term mitigation: we can temporarily increase tenant RPM by 50% for 10 minutes or apply a rolling backoff policy to accept limited bursts. (2) Long-term: recommend client jitter + ack-based reconnects and enabling streaming keepalive to avoid large reconnect waves.
Tom (SRE): Also check client's retry behavior — ensure exponential backoff + capped concurrency. If your SDK is opening N parallel requests per user on reconnect that's multiplicative. Suggest limiting client concurrency to 2 per user.
Jun (Acme): Can you bump for 10m? We need to restore UI while we push a client patch.
Maya (Support): I'll open a temporary quota adjustment. @ratecap-bot can you apply +50% RPM for tenant `acme` for 10m and post diff?
ratecap-bot: Applying temporary quota: tenant=acme old_rpm=12000 new_rpm=18000 duration=10m — will auto-revert. :ok_hand:
Tom (SRE): While that's happening, check server-side connection choruses: `ss -tnp | grep your-client` to confirm reconnect spikes. Also confirm no proxy-tier is retrying incorrectly (some proxies replay pending requests on TCP reconnect).
Jun (Acme): We found an nginx upstream that was re-sending pending requests when the origin closed. Patch applied to avoid double-send.
Rajat (Platform): Follow-ups: we'll add a per-tenant smooth-burst window to throttle short spikes (burst token bucket smoothing) and expose guidance in the SDK README about reconnect jitter + keepalive. Also scheduling a 1:1 to review client telemetry.
Maya (Support): Notes for handoff: cause = reconnect fanout + parallel polling + upstream proxy replay -> exceeded RPM. Immediate action = temporary +50% RPM ramp via ratecap-bot. Medium-term = client patch for jitter & concurrency, server-side smoothing.
Jun (Acme): Thanks all — the UI recovered after bump. We'll roll the client patch within the hour and follow the concurrency guidance. :thumbsup:
Tom (SRE): Please share the client metrics after the patch; we'll watch for minute-boundary spikes and check for `Retry-After` headers to ensure graceful degradation.
Maya (Support): Closing loop: created ticket INF-4239 to track SDK README update + platform smoothing feature.
Jun (Acme): +1 on ticket, appreciate the quick help.
